transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
PowerOutage.com reports around 400,000 customers remain without power,
following yesterday's high winds and heavy rain that gripped much of the mid-Atlantic.
Magdalena Stellalesco lost power in the Baltimore area,
upending Thanksgiving and her son's birthday.
We did Thanksgiving at candlelight.
We had guests over.
We kept on going.
Celebrated his birthday as well at candlelight.
So it was, yeah, something different.
Stellalesco says Baltimore Gas and Electric expects power to be back on by around 11 o'clock tonight.
Flight delays and cancellations persist as the nation's air travel industry continues to work its way through yesterday's severe weather,
and PR's John Stoleness reports.
The outlook is better today, as the nor'easter that caused so many headaches on Thanksgiving has moved away from the East Coast.
The flight tracking website FlightAware reported a total of 462 flight cancellations in the U.S. Thanksgiving Day,
with over 2,800 delays.
Airports in Washington, D.C. and New York were most affected, and were still seeing delays on Friday.
The heaviest travel day of the Thanksgiving weekend will be on Sunday.
The Transportation Safety Administration projects they will screen more than 3 million passengers at U.S. airports that day.
John Stoleness, NPR News.
Today is the busiest shopping day of the year, but many people wonder about the quality of the deals and discounts.
NPR's Alina Seljuk reports.
Several groups this year released research suggesting that many sales only masquerade as discounts,
and shopping experts always recommend knowing in advance what the typical price is for something you plan to buy on Black Friday.
Adobe Analytics tracks actual spending and prices, specifically online,
and the group predicts that Black Friday is likely to have the biggest discounts for toys, clothes, appliances, furniture and televisions.
Meanwhile, Cyber Monday might have better discounts for computers and other electronics.
Top discounts are expected to be from 18 to 30 percent. Alina Seljuk, NPR News.
The Norwegian airline Norse Atlantic has filed for bankruptcy.
As Esme Nicholson reports, the airline was unable to resolve financial difficulties caused by soaring fuel prices.
Budget carrier Norse Atlantic Airways has stopped all flights and services effective immediately.
This impacts a number of long-haul routes from Europe to the U.S., Asia and Africa.
Parent company Norse Atlantic ASA said in a statement that insolvency was unavoidable despite extensive efforts to find a solution.
It also apologized to passengers, employees and partners.
With the most recent barrel prices up 72 percent year on year, the airline could no longer afford jet fuel.
Attempts to find short-term financing failed this week.
You're listening to NPR. U.S. lawmakers are investigating how children might be exposed to online predators on the gaming platform Roblox.
At a Senate hearing this month, two survivors told lawmakers they were groomed and sexually abused by men they met on the site.
NPR's Ritu Chatterjee reports.
One of the witnesses at the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing was Woody Doe, a Marine Corps veteran. Doe, who used a partial pseudonym at the hearing, told lawmakers that as a child he loved Roblox.
Like millions of children, I discovered Roblox and quickly became hooked.
But he alleged that the platform exposed him to a predator.
Eleven. That's how old I was when I was groomed and sexually assaulted by a man I met on Roblox.
He's among dozens of survivors who've sued Roblox for its role in exposing them to predators.
Roblox told NPR that safety has been central to the company, and it now requires users to verify their age to communicate with others, and only allows kids of similar ages to communicate with each other.
Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.
Vice President J.D. Vance is downplaying the possibility that NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang might be pardoned by President Trump. Huang resigned from his post earlier this month after admitting to extramarital affairs, including with a woman who had contact with Chinese intelligence.
Huang, who was reinstated, in part due to the president's urging, is set to appear before lawmakers next week for a closed-door interview as well as a public hearing.
President Trump told the New York Post that pardoning Huang is an option, but likely unnecessary.
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Baltimore resident Magdalena Stellalesco describes candlelit Thanksgiving after power outage from mid-Atlantic storms
PowerOutage.com reports about 400,000 customers still without power after mid-Atlantic high winds and rain
Flight delays and cancellations persist after Thanksgiving nor'easter; Transportation Safety Administration projects heavy Sunday travel
Adobe Analytics predicts Black Friday discounts of 18 to 30 percent, shoppers urged to check typical prices
Norwegian budget airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, halts all flights amid soaring jet fuel prices
Senate hearing examines child exposure to online predators on Roblox, survivor Woody Doe testifies
Vice President Vance downplays possibility of President Trump pardoning NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang
